---
title: "Extensions"
extensions: [embed, tabset]
---

qmd-fast keeps a lean core and pushes power to **extensions**. An extension is a
folder under `_extensions/<name>/` with an `_extension.yml` manifest plus whatever
CSS, JS, and templates it ships. There are three things an extension can do, from
simplest to most powerful: contribute a **format/theme**, declare
**shortcodes**, and register a client-side **enhancer**.

## Format & theme extensions

A format extension is selected by name in the front matter:

```yaml
format:
  liquid-glass-revealjs:   # <name>-<base>, base is revealjs or html
    slide-number: true
```

Its `_extensions/liquid-glass/_extension.yml` is a flat manifest that contributes
includes, a theme, and resources:

```yaml
name: Liquid Glass
theme: [dark, liquid-glass.css]    # .css layers inlined ahead of the deck
resources: [liquid-glass.js]       # copied next to the output / served in preview
head: liquid-glass-head.html       # = include-in-header (also: body-start, body-end)
body-end: liquid-glass-init.html
```

The contribution keys mirror the [project config](../reference/configuration.qmd)
(`head`/`body-start`/`body-end`/`resources`/`css`/`theme`), so it's one
vocabulary. The contributed markup is injected **before** the document's own
front-matter `include-*`, so your page can still override the extension; a file in
`resources` is copied next to the built page (and resolved by bare name in the
live preview), so an injected `<script src="liquid-glass.js">` works in both.

The full set of recognized top-level keys is closed and small. There are five
informational metadata keys (they document the extension and have no rendering
effect): `name`, `title`, `description`, `author`, `version`. The rest are the
contributions: `theme`, `css`, `head`, `body-start`, `body-end`, `resources`,
and `shortcodes`. Anything outside that set is reported with a "did you mean …"
warning and otherwise ignored.

A failed load never takes the page down with it. If the named extension folder
has no `_extension.yml`, or the YAML doesn't parse, qmd-fast records a warning
(surfaced in the dev menu and the build log) and renders the page *without* that
extension's contributions, rather than aborting. A typo'd `extensions:` name
behaves the same way: you get a "not found" warning, and the document still
renders. The contract is loud-and-degraded, never silent-and-broken.

::: {.callout-note}
## Coming from a Quarto extension?

The nested `contributes: → formats: → <base>:` manifest shape is no longer parsed,
so flatten it: lift the keys out of that block to the top level and rename
`include-in-header` to `head`, `include-after-body` to `body-end`, and
`format-resources` to `resources`. An unflattened `contributes:` key just warns as
unknown and its contributions are ignored.
:::

## Declarative shortcodes

qmd-fast ships four shortcodes built in: `{{< include >}}` (inline another
`.qmd`), `{{< embed >}}` (a deck or doc as a framed iframe), `{{< video >}}` (a
framed screencast), and `{{< input >}}` (a reactive control feeding `{js}`
cells). You do not need an extension for any of these. The
[shortcodes reference](../reference/shortcodes.qmd) documents every argument of
each one; this section is about teaching an *extension* to add its own.

A shortcode is a `{{< name args >}}` tag in the body that expands to an HTML
template, perfect for embeds, with no JavaScript. Declare them at the top level
as a name → template map:

```yaml
shortcodes:
  youtube: '<div class="ratio"><iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/{{1}}" allowfullscreen></iframe></div>'
  callout: '<aside class="note"><strong>{{title}}</strong> {{body}}</aside>'
```

Then in any document that activates the extension:

```markdown
{{< youtube dQw4w9WgXcQ >}}
{{< callout title="Heads up" body="this expanded from a shortcode" >}}
```

Positional args fill `{{1}}`, `{{2}}`, …; named `key=value` args (quotes group
spaces) fill `{{key}}`. Expansion is line-preserving, so click-to-source still
points at the right line. Unknown `{{< … >}}` tags are left in the page verbatim
**and** reported as a located diagnostic (dev menu, build log, and `qmd-fast
check`), so a typo'd name shows up rather than shipping silently as literal text.

## Client enhancers

For anything interactive, ship a `.js` file (via `resources` or a
`body-end` include) that registers an **enhancer** through the public API. The
one method you call is `register`:

```js
window.qmdEnhancers.register(function (root) {
  root.querySelectorAll('.timestamp:not([data-done])').forEach(function (el) {
    el.dataset.done = '1';
    el.textContent = new Date(el.dataset.epoch * 1000).toLocaleString();
  });
});
```

`register(fn)` takes a single function `fn(root)`, where `root` is the DOM
subtree to decorate. It returns the registry, so calls chain.

### When your enhancer runs

`fn(root)` fires at three moments:

- **On the initial render.** In the static build, on `DOMContentLoaded`; in the
  live preview, when the first `full_render` mounts the body. `root` is the
  `#qmd-root` mount container (so a descendant `querySelectorAll` reaches the
  whole document).
- **After every incremental block op.** When you save the `.qmd`, the preview
  sends `update` / `insert` / `remove` ops that swap individual blocks, then
  re-runs *all* registered enhancers over the whole `#qmd-root` again. (A
  metadata-only `set_meta` op, which just repatches `data-sourcepos`, does not
  re-run them: the content is unchanged.)
- **Once immediately on late registration.** If your script loads after the page
  is already mounted (the usual case for a `body-end` include), `register`
  invokes your `fn` once right away so it catches up on the existing DOM.

::: {.callout-important}
## Enhancers MUST be idempotent

Because a single `insert` re-runs every enhancer over the *entire* `#qmd-root`,
your `fn` will revisit blocks it already decorated. Running twice must be a
no-op: guard each element with a `data-` attribute (the `:not([data-done])`
filter above), or you will stack duplicate buttons, listeners, and nodes on every
keystroke. This is the same registry the built-in copy buttons, lightbox, and
Mermaid renderer use, and they all guard exactly this way, so a third-party
enhancer is indistinguishable from core's. Errors thrown inside an enhancer are
caught and logged to the console; one broken enhancer never stops the others.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Diagnostics, not silence

A typo'd extension name, a malformed `_extension.yml`, or an unknown manifest key
is reported in the dev menu and the build log, so a broken extension never fails
silently.
:::

## Activating extensions

A *format/theme* extension is selected by `format:` (above). A *shortcode* or
*enhancer* extension is switched on with the `extensions:` front-matter list:

```yaml
---
title: "My post"
extensions: [embed, tabset]   # vendored under <project>/_extensions/
---
```

Extensions are found in the nearest `_extensions/` walking up to the project root,
so a whole book or site can share one `_extensions/` folder.

## See them in action

This chapter activates `extensions: [embed, tabset]`, and both extensions below
are *live*: the same `embed` and `tabset` folders sit under this book's
`_extensions/`.

A `{{< youtube … >}}` shortcode from the **embed** extension expands to a
responsive player (it plays once the page is *served*: some videos block the
`file://` referrer of a locally-opened build):

{{< youtube jNQXAC9IVRw >}}

…and the **tabset** enhancer turns a `::: {.panel-tabset}` of headings into tabs
(click between them). Note `.panel-tabset` is actually **built into core** (the
tablist is emitted server-side with ARIA roles and core ships its own `tabset.js`);
the bundled `tabset` extension here re-implements it purely to demonstrate the
enhancer API, so you do not need an extension to use tabsets:

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Python

```python
print("hello from the Python tab")
```

### R

```r
cat("hello from the R tab")
```

### Notes

Each heading inside the `panel-tabset` div becomes a tab; the enhancer registers
through `window.qmdEnhancers`, exactly like core's built-ins.

:::
